steps.description: Filter genes with filterByExpr (grouped by condition), normalize with TMM (edgeR::calcNormFactors), and fit a limma-voom fixed-effects linear model on the case-vs-control contrast with an explicit reference level (control) — do not rely on alphabetical factor ordering. plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE with effect-size triage
plan.analytical_narrative: 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired, single-batch whole-blood Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 120 samples). At n=60/group, DESeq2/edgeR's negative-binomial assumption is known to inflate false positives in large population cohorts (Mishra et al. 2022), so the differential expression test uses limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model instead, following TMM normalization and filterByExpr filtering, with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test run in parallel as a distribution-free robustness check on the same contrast. The research question explicitly separates statistical significance from practical magnitude, so multiple testing uses BH-adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05 together with a TREAT test against an explicit log2FC threshold (0.5, a conventional 'meaningfully different' cutoff for blood transcriptomics) rather than a post-hoc fold-change filter on the point estimate, which would not control the false discovery rate for the threshold question. QC precedes the model (blinded VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) since batch is reported as single/none but sample-level outliers or hidden structure must still be checked before trusting the model. Enrichment runs on the full ranked gene list (camera + fgsea) against Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human gene sets staged in the reference store, using the moderated t-statistic as the ranking metric, with results reported as hypotheses given known method-dependence of enrichment results. The final report explicitly separates the 'differs' question (adjusted p<0.05) from the 'differs by an amount that matters' question (TREAT-significant genes above the fold-change threshold), sorting the significant table by effect size as the population-cohort guidance requires.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If each group holds 50 or more samples, use limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model for the differential expression test. In a population cohort the sample-to-sample variation does not obey the negative binomial model, and DESeq2 and edgeR then report many false positives, even on permuted labels. The linear model on the log counts with precision weights keeps the false discovery rate closer to the nominal level than the count models, but it also exceeds it on some data. The paper recommends the Wilcoxon rank-sum test at a large sample size. State this caution in the report, and give the Wilcoxon test or a permutation check as the control.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
